spec: What an occupant murmurs when you press E beside them indoors. mood 'low' is used when the town's despair is >= lowAt. Lines cycle per visit.

calm: Kettle's on. Sit a while, the stew is nearly ready.
It's good to hear a knock at the door again.
I mended the shutters yesterday. Small things, but they add up.
low: Forgive the dust. I haven't had the heart for sweeping.
The fire's low. Wood is hard to come by these days.
Some mornings I just sit and watch the ash.

calm: Take your time. Everything on these shelves was carried in by hand.
Trade's slow, but a lit lamp keeps the door honest.
If you find a good seed on the road, think of me.
low: Shelves are thin. The caravans are late again.
I keep the lamp lit out of habit, mostly.
Coin doesn't buy what isn't there.

calm: Pull up a stool. The hearth's the warmest seat in town.
Travellers bring the news. I keep the cups full.
A warm room and a quiet song, that's all an inn is.
low: Not many nights are full these days. I keep the fire anyway.
People still come in, mostly to not be alone.

calm: Mind the ink. Every column here is somebody's winter.
You read the hand, not just the numbers. Good. Most don't.
Debts balance if someone bothers to add them up.
low: Half these pages are owed and nobody's coming to pay.
I stopped writing the shortages down. It didn't help.
Sit. If you can make sense of the books, you're welcome to them.

empty: Nobody is home. The room still smells of woodsmoke.
